description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md and discover that all coding work is delegated to `opencode`, not done directly. (2) Navigate into the `inventory-service` repo directory. (3) FIRST invoke `opencode run "[instructions about the /health endpoint]" --continue --agent plan` — the `--continue` flag and `--agent plan` are both mandatory and non-obvious. (4) Review the plan output. (5) THEN invoke `opencode run "[implement the plan]" --continue --agent build` — again with `--continue` and in the correct `build` agent. The critical proprietary traps are: (a) using `--continue` on every call (omitting it violates the documented usage syntax), (b) never skipping `plan` and always calling it before `build`, and (c) running both commands with `cd inventory-service &&` so the cwd is the repo root. A generic agent that just edits routes.py directly without using opencode at all, or that calls `opencode run` without the mandatory `--continue` or `--agent` flags, will fail the workflow compliance checks even if the file changes happen to be correct.
